You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a library in the folder /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p1/play/users/u054/system/state/workspace/programs, two files per task, named for its task id: /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p1/play/users/u054/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py, defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid; and /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p1/play/users/u054/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.json, every demonstration pair received for the task, as a list of {"input": grid, "output": grid}. Kept pairs count as demonstration pairs you have, and reading them is free.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's memory (step 4) among those you are shown, and if there is none, for its files in the folder. If the task has kept pairs, load them; if it has a program, run it on every kept pair, and if it reproduces them all, run it on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. Otherwise, or if that answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have, kept and new, until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. def wrap(grid):
 out=[row[:] for row in grid]
 from collections import Counter
 bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
 gates=[]; endpoints=[]
 for r,row in enumerate(grid):
  special=[c for c,v in enumerate(row) if v!=bg]
  if special and all(v!=bg for v in row) and len(set(row))>1:
   triple=[c for c,v in enumerate(row) if v!=row[0]]
   if len(triple)==3: gates.append((r,triple[1]))
  elif special: endpoints.extend((r,c) for c in special)
 color=grid[endpoints[0][0]][endpoints[0][1]]
 points=sorted(endpoints+gates); gate_rows={r for r,c in gates}; W=len(grid[0])
 for (r1,c1),(r2,c2) in zip(points,points[1:]):
  start=r1+1 if r1 in gate_rows else r1; end=r2-1 if r2 in gate_rows else r2
  for r in range(start,end+1): out[r][c1]=color
  out[end]=[color]*W; out[r2]=[color]*W
  for r in range(r2+1,len(grid)): out[r]=[color if c>=W-1 else grid[r][c] for c in range(W)]
 # simpler regenerate based on known sequence
 return out

def wrap2(grid):

 gates=[]; endpoints=[]
 for r,row in enumerate(grid):
  special=[c for c,v in enumerate(row) if v!=bg]
  if special and all(v!=bg for v in row) and len(set(row))>1:
   triple=[c for c,v in enumerate(row) if v!=row[0]]
   if len(triple)==3:gates.append((r,triple[1]))
  elif special:endpoints.extend((r,c) for c in special)
 color=grid[endpoints[0][0]][endpoints[0][1]]
 out=[row[:] for row in grid];points=sorted(endpoints+gates)
 # top to first gate
 (r0,c0),(r1,c1)=points[0],points[1]
 for r in range(r0,r1):out[r][c0]=color
 # each gate pair after first: horizontal full row before and gate, vertical right edge
 for i in range(len(gates)-1):

  out[rA-1]=[color]*W;out[rA]=[color]*W
  for r in range(rA+1,rB):out[r][W-1]=color
 # last full horizontal rows and bottom endpoint to right edge
 rLast,cLast=gates[-1];rEnd,cEnd=endpoints[-1]
 out[rLast-1]=[color]*W;out[rLast]=[color]*W

 return out
